findings.title: SQL injection in migration via interpolated host value

The value of h comes from the legacy embeddable_hosts site setting (one per line) and is used unescaped. A value containing a single quote (or other SQL meta-characters) would either break the migration or, if the site setting was modified outside of Rails, allow arbitrary SQL execution during migrate. Use parameterized SQL (e.g., ActiveRecord::Base.connection.exec_query with a bound host, or a model.create!) instead of string interpolation.

The store's `_hydrateEmbedded` requires the pluralized array to be present in the root to look up and hydrate objects from the IDs. As a result, the admin embedding page will always show an empty table even when embeddable hosts exist. Change to `embed: :objects` (or omit the embed option) so the full embeddable_hosts array is included in the response.

Lowercase the parameter: `where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase).first`.

Either extend the adapter to invoke the callback, or drop the dead code to avoid future confusion.

Because the input is inside `{{#if editing}}`, that selector does not exist in the rendered DOM, so on some browsers the focus falls back to body and subsequent keypresses after Cancel can land outside the component.
